regime: Risk-On Continuation, Equities Extend (Crude Breaks Down, Fed Eve)
summary: Risk-on kept going. The Nasdaq dipped below its opening range early, that break failed, and price reversed into a clean trend-up day, closing 29,804, up 1.14 percent, well above its trend stop and its 50-hour average. The S&P confirmed, up 0.55 percent to 7,756.25, also above both lines. Gold firmed a second day, up 1.04 percent to 4,072.9, with its trailing stop holding long, though it is still under its 50-hour average. Crude went the other way: it lost its long stop, flipped short, and closed 100.23, down 1.03 percent. VIX fell again to 17.52, now well under 20, one session before the Fed decision.

event.actual: Risk-on continuation. The Nasdaq and S&P extended above their ATR trailing stops and 50-hour averages; VIX fell under 18; gold firmed a second day; crude lost its stop and flipped short.

risk.openRisk: Measured. Index trend-longs are live, but keep size small into Wednesday's Fed decision.
risk.note: Throttle holds at REDUCED into the Fed decision. Equities extended their trend-longs and VIX eased under 18, which on its own would ease the throttle toward NORMAL, but the rate decision is Wednesday Oct 28 at 2 pm Eastern, so size stays measured into a known binary. No drawdown flags and the loss budget is full. Gold is still below its 4,092 average, so that turn is unconfirmed. Crude flipped short, so 101.89 is now resistance with the 99.44 low below. Week ahead: Wednesday's FOMC is the catalyst; expect pre-decision drift then a fast reaction.

psychology: Today's lesson is in the first move. Price broke the opening range to the downside early, which pulled in shorts, then it reversed and trended up the rest of the day. A first move that fails is information. The reclaim, not the break, was the real tell. Tomorrow the Fed decides at 2 pm Eastern, and the first spike after the release often reverses the same way. Wait for acceptance, two hourly closes beyond a level, before you commit. Patience beats prediction into a known event.
